messages:
maria_customer: Hey team — running into an intermittent issue with the Python streaming client. We open a SSE stream to /v1/stream, get a few chunks, then the connection emits a 401 and closes. This only happens when our auth refresh kicks in (~90s).

maria_customer: Minimal repro: start stream with short-lived token (expires in 120s), keep reading the iterator. After ~70–100s we see: 
```
[INFO] stream chunk: 'Hello, wor'
[INFO] stream chunk: 'ld'
[ERROR] SSE connection closed: status=401 body='{"type":"auth_error","message":"token expired"}' X-Request-ID=req_8f3a
```

alex_support: Thanks — can you paste the exact client flow? Are you doing a token refresh that swaps Authorization on the same socket? Also want the X-Request-ID and headers if possible.

maria_customer: We refresh in a background coroutine and update our global bearer token. We do not re-open the socket because the SDK's iterator keeps using the same HTTP connection. Sample request (we use requests + sseclient):
```
POST /v1/stream
Authorization: Bearer <short-token>
Accept: text/event-stream
Body: {"model":"redwood/fast-1","input":"..."}
```
Then our refresh swaps the token in-process. We only see the 401 in the server logs and the connection dies. X-Request-ID is req_8f3a.

alex_support: Got it. Reproduced locally with your token TTL and our python sseclient wrapper. Confirming we get a 401 from the server and the SSE stream closes. tagging @kai_eng-runtime to check server-side behavior. :thinking: 

kai_eng-runtime: Looking at logs for req_8f3a — server validation fails on a per-chunk check after a heartbeat. Currently the authorization check runs on each read boundary; if token expired we emit a 401 and close. That's by design for short TTLs but we didn't consider in-flight refresh semantics with persistent SSE connections.

jess_eng-ml: This explains partial outputs — app receives some chunks but can't resume. From quality standpoint we should avoid mid-stream hard closes if we can resume. Two options: (1) server grace window (~30s) to accept recently-expired tokens for existing streams, (2) expose an explicit resume protocol (stream_id + resume_token) so SDK can reconnect and request continuation. Both have tradeoffs for security and correctness.

alex_support: Short term workaround for customers: give streaming tokens longer TTLs than the expected stream duration or proactively refresh and re-open the stream before expiry. But we need a long-term fix in the SDK/runtime.

kai_eng-runtime: Agreed. Implementation plan proposal:
- Server: accept a 10s grace window for existing SSE connections where the connection stays open despite token expiry; emit an SSE event `event: auth_refresh_needed` to notify client.
- SDK: catch 401 mid-stream and attempt an automatic reconnect using a resume param that includes last-acknowledged token index.

maria_customer: Would automatic reconnect work without creating duplicates? We rely on idempotent continuation.

jess_eng-ml: We'll need the model/runtime to provide deterministic resume points (byte offsets or generation checkpoint IDs). For now, SDK reconnect should request only the missing suffix (server-side replay). That requires minor server support.

alex_support: Can you prototype a Python SDK patch that on HTTP 401 reads the last "event: chunk" id and calls POST /v1/stream?resume_from=<id> with new Authorization, retrying up to 2x? If resume not accepted, surface an error.

kai_eng-runtime: I'll spec the resume token shape. It will be small (stream_id + seq_num). We can implement a short-term grace-window and an opt-in header `X-Resume-Enabled: 1` so we can A/B test.

maria_customer: That would work for us. Thanks.

alex_support: For tracking — creating a bug and assigning to eng-runtime. P0 for now since this affects streaming reliability for short-lived auth.

deploy-bot: Created issue INFR-4932: "python sdk: handle 401 mid-stream and support resume" assigned to kai_eng-runtime. Patch branch: fix/stream-resume-auth.

kai_eng-runtime: I'll pick this up. Plan: implement 10s grace window + server resume endpoint + SDK fallback handling. Target: patch in staging by EOD, canary next day.

maria_customer: Appreciate it. We'll test against staging and validate no duplicates. Will report back in this thread. :thumbsup: 

alex_support: Also adding a note to docs: recommend token TTL > longest stream or use refresh+reopen pattern until we ship the fix.

maria_customer: FYI — here's a minimal python instructive snippet I used to reproduce: 
```python
import requests, sseclient
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream', headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {short_token}', 'Accept':'text/event-stream'}, json={'model':'redwood/fast-1', 'input':'hi'})
client = sseclient.SSEClient(resp)
for event in client.events():
    print('evt', event.data)
# after ~90s the loop raises/ends with 401
```

alex_support: Great repro — that will help QA. Marking follow-ups: (1) server grace window, (2) resume API, (3) python SDK patch to auto-reconnect on 401 and dedupe.

kai_eng-runtime: I'll post a link to the staging build here once ready.

maria_customer: Standing by to test. Thanks all!
